claim: Exact scenario revisions can be evaluated against one verified immutable policy version through a bounded, sequential, persistent, pause/resume/retry queue using optional local inference or native-approved API routes.
verified: Queue definitions bind one verified policy version, exact scenario revisions, one provider/model route, unique run/result identities, creator attribution, at most 200 items, at most three attempts, and a two-megabyte aggregate revision bound
Definitions, controls, item attempts, failures, and results use strict peer-namespaced collaborative records with exact replay idempotence, collision/fork rejection, and creator-only controls

A begin event is persisted before provider work; result plus completion event commit in one Yjs transaction; a crash after begin reopens as interrupted and resumes the same attempt without another begin
The runner executes one item at a time, rejects duplicate in-process runners, emits progress heartbeats no slower than 30 seconds, and enforces a hard two-minute item deadline
Pause/cancel abort the active provider best-effort without erasing progress; provider failures are sanitized, bounded, and explicit; retry cannot exceed the job ceiling
Completed items cannot run again and exact completion replay produces no second collaborative update
Local, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and xAI routes share one strict handled/unhandled/uncertain contract with mandatory response, rationale, uncertainty, and route provenance
Remote execution prepares only one exact policy version and one exact scenario revision for each native Send once approval; adapters expose no tools or ambient source authority
The scenario workspace creates paused queues, selects scenarios/routes, controls creator-owned execution, and shows every shared result while preserving manual/no-AI work
Research-state/MCP inspection exposes only queue/status/route/item/integrity counts and orphan IDs; policy/scenario/result/rationale/uncertainty bodies are omitted with secret canaries
Focused product/domain/runtime/runner/inspection tests and the production frontend build pass
limitations: No live paid-provider call, model-quality benchmark, or semantic correctness claim is included; provider behavior is injected and deterministic.
Researcher identity and timestamps are installation/caller supplied and are not authenticated or trusted across installs.
No packaged two-physical-install queue convergence or crash-at-IndexedDB-durability run is included.
Remote queues wait for native Send once approval per item; unattended blanket disclosure is intentionally not implemented.
An offline collaborator change not yet delivered cannot be predicted; stale exact scenario revisions require a new queue.
Baseline comparison/export is tracked separately as P-31, and the open scenario-pack schema is tracked as P-33.
